why: The criterion-content oracle compares predicate-registry.json to tools/phase_content.py, a file the author controls, so the mutation that defeats it is not a mutation of the registry at all. The recheck replaced ONE spec entry in the derivation, ran author_phase_content.py, and measured exit 0 with 268,829 checks and 27 of 27 negative fixtures still rejecting -- with the whole G2-01 defect back: no fulfillment_ref, no `delivered` binding, no obligation states, correlation on `performed`. This fixture performs exactly that, and requires the validator to reject it. What rejects it is contracts/pinned-conjuncts.json, which is hand-written and which author_phase_content.py neither reads nor writes: regenerating cannot satisfy a pin, only stating the requirement can.
note: A positive control is built in and is not optional: if the regeneration step fails, the runner reports FAIL rather than counting the fixture as rejected, because a mutation that never reached the validator proves nothing. And if this fixture ever fails for a reason OTHER than the pin -- the runner checks the message -- the pin has been replaced by something weaker that happens to also refuse.
